claims.explanation: PI-828 is a PI3K/mTOR-pathway inhibitor, and its selective killing pattern tracks with dependence on PI3K/AKT/mTOR signaling rather than with any single lineage. Sensitive lines are enriched for upstream pathway activation (PIK3CA mutation, PTEN loss, EGFR/BRAF/NRAS activation) and for TP53/CDKN2A loss that permits apoptosis, whereas lines with intact PTEN or alternative survival signaling are relatively protected. The transcriptional signature (FOXO up, MYC/PLK1/CCNA2 down) is consistent with PI3K/AKT/mTOR inhibition.

features.basis: Activating PIK3CA mutations predict PI3K-pathway dependence; enriched in sensitive lines (SNUC5, KYSE510, SNU840)
PTEN loss relieves PI3K/AKT restraint; seen in sensitive 786O and other pathway-activated lines
TP53 loss permits apoptosis after PI3K inhibition; near-universal in sensitive lines
Cell-cycle checkpoint loss enhances sensitivity to PI3K/mTOR inhibition; enriched in sensitive melanoma/Ewing lines
EGFR-driven RTK signaling feeds PI3K/AKT; seen in sensitive NCIH1650
BRAF activation engages PI3K/AKT; enriched in sensitive melanoma/colorectal lines
RAS-driven tumors can depend on PI3K effectors; seen in sensitive OV7, SNU410
NF1 loss hyperactivates RAS/PI3K; seen in sensitive BICR6, LOXIMVI
Intact PTEN restrains PI3K signaling; PTEN-mutant lines are less represented among resistant lines
Low PI3K pathway output reduces dependence on the drug target
Virtual cell shows MYC upregulation and cell-cycle gene downregulation, consistent with PI3K/mTOR inhibition
FOXO4 upregulation in virtual cell indicates AKT inhibition and FOXO nuclear activity
